# dsh-opencode-go-catalog

A live-maintained OpenCode Go model catalog for DeepSeek Harness
(DSH). Membership is rebuilt from t

he live roster plus the docs endpoint table on every sync — new
models appear, retired ones drop out
, no hand work. A curated snapshot stays as the offline fallback.
**Status:** 0.2.0 · auto membership · 33 models live (2026-10-13), incl. **Cat Jam Free** (`cat-jam-

## Why
The built-in `opencode-go` route of `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-pi-ai` serves a static catalog shipped in
`@earendil-works/pi-ai` (30 models at the time of writing) that never refreshes itself — new models

like Step 5 or Cat Jam are missing until upstream bumps the dependency. See
Discussion #3957.

This plugin never touches the built-in route. It manages three sibling routes through the
official `
settings.mutate` seam:
| Route | Protocol | Examples |
| `opencode-go-extras` | `openai-completions` | Cat Jam Free, Step 5 Preview Free, GLM-5.3, LongCat,

MiMo, Kimi, DeepSeek |
| `opencode-go-responses` | `openai-responses` | GPT-5.6/6 Luna, Grok 4.6/4.

7, Muse Spark 1.2/1.3 |
| `opencode-go-messages` | `anthropic-messages` | Claude Haiku 5.5, Qwen3.8,

1.3 |
| `opencode-go-messages` | `anthropic-messages` | Claude Haiku 5.5, Qwen3.8, MiniMax M2.7/M3 |

The split is mandatory, not stylistic: some Go models are *Responses-only* (a chat-completions
reque

st answers with a bare `500` or `401 "not supported for format oa-compat"`), others are
*Messages-on
ly*. One route = one protocol.

**Why not put the extra models on the built-in route?** Source-verified against `dsh-llm-pi-ai`:
`re

solveRouteModels` computes a model's protocol as `request.api ?? base?.api ?? routeApi` — an
`api` f

ield *on a model entry* is never read. A model the shipped catalog does not describe
therefore needs

the **route-level** `api`, and setting that routes `opencode-go` through
`createProvider()` over a

*single* protocol (the catalog provider is only reused while
`spec.api === undefined`), losing both

the three-protocol dispatch and pi-ai's session-header
wrapper. On top of that, any `models` list *r

eplaces* the served catalog. The built-in route stays
untouched.
## How it works

1. **Registry** — `https://models.opencode.ai/api.json` (keyless, ETag cache + last-good fallback)
s

upplies name, limits, input modalities, and `reasoning_options` per model.
2. **Roster** — `https://

opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/models` (keyless) says which IDs exist *right now*.
3. **Protocol oracle** — `

https://opencode.ai/docs/go/` (since 2026-10-19 redirecting to
`/v2/docs/console/go/`) carries an en

dpoint table per model ID in either path shape
(`…/go/v1/chat/completions` or `…/go/<lane>/v1/chat/c

ompletions`, plus `/responses` and
`/messages`). See The protocol oracle.
4. Membership is then `ros

ter ∩ registry ∩ protocol-known`, minus the veto list. On startup, on an
interval (default 4 h), and

on `/opencode-go-sync` the three sibling routes are written via
`settings.mutate`.
5. **Fail-safe.*

* The auto mode refuses to write, and the curated snapshot in `catalog/models.json`
is served unchan

ged, when
- the roster or the oracle is unavailable (network, docs redesign), or
- fewer than `minAu

toModels` models resolve, or
- fewer than `minAutoRatio` (default 60 %) of the last adopted set reso

lve — this catches a
*degraded* source that would otherwise quietly empty half the picker and stamp

the missing IDs
as retired.

A single route that comes out empty is not fatal either: `llm-pi-ai` rejects a route with
`resolves

no models`, and because all three routes go into one `settings.mutate`, one empty group
would block

the healthy groups too — so that route is served from the snapshot and reported in
`status.json` (`a

uto.snapshotRoutes`). A network outage or a docs redesign can therefore never
empty the picker. Miss

ing capacities are never invented — the field is omitted and `needsReview`
is reported, so `llm-pi-a

i` applies its own route defaults (262144 / 32768).
6. The module never throws during boot, never ed

its `node_modules`, and never reads or writes
credentials (it only references the `OPENCODE_GO_API_K
EY` name, same as the built-in route).

**Hand-added models do not survive.** `settings.mutate` persists into the profile's
[该节后续省略]
## Installation

Prerequisites: DSH running, an OpenCode Go subscription with a working key
(`OPENCODE_GO_API_KEY` al
ready configured — if the built-in `opencode-go` route works, you are set).

**Via Plugin Market** (once listed): Settings → Plugin Market → search
`dsh-opencode-go-catalog` → o

ne-click install → restart → open the model picker.
Expect three new groups (*OpenCode Go extras / r
esponses / messages*) next to the built-in one.

**Manual**: copy this folder to `<profile>/node_modules/dsh-opencode-go-catalog`, add
[该节后续省略]
## Security
- **No secrets:** the plugin never reads, writes, logs, or ships credentials. `OPENCODE_GO_API_KEY`

appears only as a *name reference*, exactly like the built-in route. Verified by pre-commit sweep.
-

**Network:** only three public, keyless endpoints (`models.opencode.ai/api.json`,
`opencode.ai/zen/

go/v1/models`, `opencode.ai/docs/go/`), each with timeout + cache + offline
fallback to snapshot val

ues.
- **Zero dependencies**, no `@deepseek-ai/dsh*` peers (the install gate cannot refuse it),
no s
hell hooks, fail-safe boot.
## Compatibility

Built against DSH `0.2.0-rc.2` behavior (static pi-ai catalog, `settings.mutate` seam, optional
comm
and registry). Pure ESM, Node ≥ 18.
